builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
summary: The method replaces full-precision n-gram embedding tables with low-precision (four-bit or lower) quantized tables, optionally reallocating the saved memory to larger tables. The cost is a quantization and possible short fine-tuning pipeline plus a small quality loss, which grows sharply below four bits and is only partially recoverable by fine-tuning. Adoption can fail if the target model lacks n-gram embedding tables entirely, if sub-four-bit precision is required (where degradation is larger), or if downstream task regressions appear that the paper's limited evaluation did not cover.
rationale: The technique is sound and quantified, but it applies only to models that already contain n-gram embedding tables, which most models the reader can run or fine-tune on a single 24 GB GPU do not have, making it relevant mainly as a serving-time option to watch rather than an immediate adoption.
technique: Low-bit quantization of n-gram embedding tables

claims.statement: The method replaces full-precision n-gram embedding tables with low-precision (four-bit or lower) quantized tables, optionally reallocating the saved memory to larger tables. The cost is a quantization and possible short fine-tuning pipeline plus a small quality loss, which grows sharply below four bits and is only partially recoverable by fine-tuning. Adoption can fail if the target model lacks n-gram embedding tables entirely, if sub-four-bit precision is required (where degradation is larger), or if downstream task regressions appear that the paper's limited evaluation did not cover.

Four-bit n-gram tables save approximately 75% of table memory while preserving over 99% of the validation-loss improvement; on large existing models, low-bit tables save 47-55% of table memory with perplexity increases under 1.2%.
